captions.facebook:
FINANCIAL EDUCATION · Education edition

Gross pay, tax and take-home pay

Gross pay is the pay agreed with an employer before tax. Take-home (net) pay is what reaches the bank account after tax and other deductions.

A household budget is built on take-home pay.

Hypothetical example: if $1,000 of gross pay leaves $800 after tax, the household has $800 to plan with.

Tax rules differ by country and change over time. The official source is the tax authority, such as the ATO in Australia or the Income Tax Department in India.

Learn. Understand. Stay Informed.
